resources.string: To detect if a power menu is opened, Officer needs accessibility settings. You can be rest assured that this setting has no other malicious intent.
Officer uses this privilege to put your screen to sleep in case someone tries to power off your phone from the lock screen.

On Android 13 and above, accessibility permission is blocked by default for applications that are not downloaded from the Google Play Store. However, you can still enable it by following these steps:

 1. Try to enable the accessibility by clicking on "Grant Accessibility Permission" button above.
 2. You will most probably see a "Restricted Setting" message. Make sure you open the popup dialog saying "For your security, this setting is currently unavailable".
 3. Only after this, go to App info page of this app and click on three dots menu in top right corner.
 4. Click "Allow restricted settings".


Note: This is an open source application. Rest assured that this setting has no other malicious intent.
Turn screen off automatically for a specific time if tried to power off from lock screen. Less convenient, but more secure.

When this setting is on, if someone opens the power menu from the lock screen, the screen will turn off automatically. A timer will then start, and during this time, the screen will turn off again if turned on. Once the timer ends, you can use your phone normally. If someone tries to open the power menu again, the timer restarts. This makes it much harder for a thief to shut down the phone before it locks.

Different phone manufacturers have different event triggers which get broadcast when the power menu is opened. Hence, there is no one-size-fits all solution. Trigger the power menu right now, and the app will detect a few related events which were broadcasted. Try out all the options in the list of events below and select an option which works for your device.

Officer is an open source app, which helps in locating your phone in case of theft. No root or Shizuku required.

Usually, if you lose your phone, you can locate it using the Google\'s \'Find my Device\' feature. However, that only works if your device is not switched off. Thieves take advantage of this, and they power off your phone to prevent tracking.

This app will prevent powering off your phone from the lock screen. It uses a work-around where in case anyone tries to open the power menu from the lock screen, it will put the display to sleep. But don\'t worry, if YOU want to power off your phone, you can unlock your screen and proceed as usual.
Enter the phone number, your desired text message and the SIM card network to be used. This number will be receiving your text message. Make sure you include the country code in the number.
Append the Google Maps location link to the SMS content.

Decide how many times you would like the app to ignore powering off attempts before sending the SMS. This is useful for preventing accidental alerts. The ignore count resets when you unlock your device.
